questions.stem: What does housekeeping refer to in the data world?
options: The physical cleaning of server rooms
The routine maintenance, organisation and management tasks needed to ensure data quality, integrity and efficiency
The onboarding of new data analysts
The negotiation of cloud storage contracts
The design of new database schemas
questions.explanation: Housekeeping is the routine maintenance, organisation and management work that keeps databases, data warehouses and other storage systems in good order.

questions.stem: Approximately what proportion of operational costs can effective housekeeping measures save, on an optimistic outlook?
questions.explanation: With an optimistic outlook, effective housekeeping measures have the potential to save approximately 30% of operational costs.

questions.stem: Fixing typos in student names, standardising date formats and filling in missing grades are examples of which housekeeping task?
questions.explanation: Data cleaning identifies and rectifies errors, inconsistencies or missing values in datasets.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of data archiving as a housekeeping task?
options: Encrypting sensitive data against unauthorised access
Creating indexes to speed up queries
Documenting the meaning and format of each column
Removing data to comply with retention policies
Moving older or less frequently used data to long-term storage to optimise performance of the primary storage system
questions.explanation: Data archiving moves older or less frequently used data to long-term storage so the primary data storage system performs better.

questions.stem: Which housekeeping task accelerates data retrieval and query performance?
questions.explanation: Indexing creates indexes on databases to accelerate data retrieval and query performance, like indexing a list of books by title or author.

questions.stem: Creating a spreadsheet that documents the meaning and format of each column in a dataset is an example of which housekeeping task?
questions.explanation: Metadata management organises and documents metadata (data about data) to enhance understanding and usability.

questions.stem: How does data purging differ from general data deletion in the housekeeping examples?
options: Purging moves data to long-term storage rather than removing it
Purging removes data that is no longer needed, especially in compliance with data retention policies
Purging applies only to encrypted data
Purging is performed only before a backup
questions.explanation: Data purging removes data that is no longer needed or relevant, especially in compliance with data retention policies, such as deleting old survey responses.

questions.stem: What does the backup and recovery housekeeping task involve?
options: Deleting records of students who have left the school
Adjusting settings to improve app performance
Regularly creating copies of data to prevent loss and establishing procedures for recovery after accidental deletion or system failure
questions.explanation: Backup and recovery means regularly copying data to prevent loss and having procedures to recover it after accidental deletion or system failure.

questions.stem: Which housekeeping task is illustrated by adjusting settings in a gaming app to improve its performance on a smartphone?
questions.explanation: Performance optimisation is the fine-tuning of databases and queries to improve overall system performance; the gaming-app example illustrates it.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a data housekeeping task?
questions.explanation: Housekeeping tasks cover cleaning, deletion, backup, archiving, indexing, encryption, metadata management, purging and performance optimisation; recruitment is not among them.
